answer: A proof-of-personhood system can require each account to pass a live, randomized interview before receiving a credential. Running many identities then costs time and coordinated humans, while one credential per person limits cheap account farms. The interview is a prism that reveals varied cues across checks, yet it can exclude people with disabilities or unreliable access, and colluding participants may still deceive reviewers in a meadow of weak oversight as identities drift like a zephyr.
